data.headline: Treasury yields ease after a week of increases
data.summary: On November 16, two-, ten- and thirty-year Treasury benchmark yields slipped to 4.83%, 5.12% and 5.46%, respectively. Each remained at least 20 basis points above November 9, while overnight secured funding rose to 3.93%.

bull.text: From November 13 to 16, two-, ten- and thirty-year benchmark yields fell 5, 3 and 1 basis points, respectively, easing part of the prior increase.

bear.text: From November 9 to 16, the two-, ten- and thirty-year yields rose 27, 24 and 20 basis points, respectively. SOFR rose from 3.88% to 3.93% over the same interval.

watch.text: The ten-year minus two-year spread widened from 27 to 29 basis points between November 13 and 16. It was still narrower than November 9, when it was 32 basis points.
In the November 10 CFTC report, leveraged-fund net shorts narrowed in both E-mini S&P 500 and E-mini Russell 2000 futures compared with November 3.

limitations: The latest matched Treasury and SOFR observations are dated November 16. Benchmark Treasury yields and overnight secured funding measure different markets.
CFTC positions are a weekly futures snapshot as of November 10. The evidence does not establish current ETF returns, flows, options exposure or investor intent.
